chimneys, walks and grounds: now builds with no refusals and no off-palette blocks; make.sh exits 0 and produces build.nbt.

left: P5 interior hearth: the bricks surround at (87,1,18), (89,1,18) and (88,1,17) stays oak_planks, because the shell's floor was built there first. If the plan wants masonry at that hearth, the P5 shell (part 2) has to leave those floor cells out; this part can't write them.

Roof-to-stack meeting cells keep the roof's own blocks (27,10,21; 35,13,17; 51,11,17; 77,9,17). The chimney masonry is not laid there, so the roof is what seals the stack. Check the flashing once the roofer has seen it.

Other parts still refuse writes, outside this part and not touched: roofs 83, porches and facade ornament 23, glazing/doors/shutters 230, and rooms P3 dining room 9, P3 upper hall 5, P3 west/dormer/rear bedrooms, P5 hall and attic bedrooms, P7 living room.

waste.cost: 2 full make.sh runs, plus one parts-report.json read and one node one-liner to pull the refusals.
waste.tool: runParts should print every refusal (drop the slice(0, 8) in the log line) and expose an ownership query on the part's grid view, for example g.builtBy(x,y,z) or g.locked(x,y,z), so a part can ask before writing.

waste.what: Wrote a hand-made view that drops a chimney's writes into cells already built, duplicating the guard's rule inside the part. Also scanned the whole site (about 73k isAir calls) to build the set of taken cells.
waste.cost: One edit to grounds.mjs (about 25 lines), one import, one scan of the site per build.
waste.tool: A skip or isTaken option on chimney()/chimneyStack (for example chimneyStack(g, { ..., skip: (x,y,z) => ... })), or a runParts option that makes refused writes silent for a named part. Then the part would not need its own copy of the guard rule.

waste.cost: 1 cp and 1 mcd diff call (which worked as intended; the cost was only knowing to look for it).
waste.tool: Nothing missing: mcd diff --json already gives a verdict (NO CHANGE). A make.sh step that keeps the last build and prints the diff would make this automatic.

structured_output.summary:
chimneys, walks and grounds: now builds with no refusals and no off-palette blocks; make.sh exits 0 and produces build.nbt.
The fix: each chimney skips writes into cells an earlier part built (read once at the start of the part), so the roof stairs and P5 floor stay as they were.
The build's cells are unchanged (mcd diff vs the pre-fix build: 0 cells changed), since runParts already refused those writes.
left: P5 interior hearth: the bricks surround at (87,1,18), (89,1,18) and (88,1,17) stays oak_planks, because the shell's floor was built there first. If the plan wants masonry at that hearth, the P5 shell (part 2) has to leave those floor cells out; this part can't write them.

Roof-to-stack meeting cells keep the roof's own blocks (27,10,21; 35,13,17; 51,11,17; 77,9,17). The chimney masonry is not laid there, so the roof is what seals the stack. Check the flashing once the roofer has seen it.

Other parts still refuse writes, outside this part and not touched: roofs 83, porches and facade ornament 23, glazing/doors/shutters 230, and rooms P3 dining room 9, P3 upper hall 5, P3 west/dormer/rear bedrooms, P5 hall and attic bedrooms, P7 living room.

waste.what: Worked out which chimney wrote each of the 10 refused cells and who owned it, by reading the make.sh log and parts-report.json by hand. The log printed only 8 of the 10 entries (refusedAt is sliced to 8), so I had to read the JSON to see all of them.
waste.cost: 2 full make.sh runs, plus one parts-report.json read and one node one-liner to pull the refusals.
waste.tool: runParts should print every refusal (drop the slice(0, 8) in the log line) and expose an ownership query on the part's grid view, for example g.builtBy(x,y,z) or g.locked(x,y,z), so a part can ask before writing.

waste.what: Wrote a hand-made view that drops a chimney's writes into cells already built, duplicating the guard's rule inside the part. Also scanned the whole site (about 73k isAir calls) to build the set of taken cells.
waste.cost: One edit to grounds.mjs (about 25 lines), one import, one scan of the site per build.
waste.tool: A skip or isTaken option on chimney()/chimneyStack (for example chimneyStack(g, { ..., skip: (x,y,z) => ... })), or a runParts option that makes refused writes silent for a named part. Then the part would not need its own copy of the guard rule.

waste.what: Confirmed the build did not change by copying the old build.nbt and comparing it by hand.
